# Preserved upstream async SOURCE research inputs

`source-ced5652e` preserves nine unchanged official wa-sqlite inputs from commit
`ced5652ee7b65d22da3efeb0ef628977b64383cd`, an unreleased commit after v1.1.2.
The manifest binds upstream paths, byte counts, SHA256, Git blob identities and
upstream/local modes; the license is preserved. Upstream `dist` inputs live under
`runtime` so they remain visible source inputs rather than ignored build output.

These are reference/provenance inputs, not the selected product SOURCE provider.
The maintained web adapter uses its existing OPFS VFS through the canonical Effect
SOURCE owner; Expo, Node and the native Cloudflare host retain their existing
physical providers. The new experimental IndexedDB factory and its public async
shim were retired after consumer inventory found no maintained product or demo
caller. The default synchronous SQLite/STATE API is unchanged.

An actual Safari diagnostic of this exact upstream cohort observed strict native
journal-deletion abort, `jDelete` returning SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE, a later `jUnlock`
rejecting, and the Asyncify-backed SOURCE write remaining pending. The upstream
defect is not fixed or qualified by retiring the unused experiment. Immutable
source snapshots, bundles, provenance and native evidence remain preserved in the
repair workspace. No upstream patch, runtime rewrite or dependency fork is implied.

Input-integrity and package-payload checks still bind all nine exact paths.
Only those unchanged upstream files bypass authored style checks; provenance,
generators and this documentation retain normal checks. Their preservation does
not establish native failure acceptance for either the experiment or the actual
OPFS/Expo/Node product providers.
